title: Improvement in mitral regurgitation after alcohol septal ablation in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy: a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Anna Damlin; Andreas Rück; Mesud Mustafic; Rebecka Jandér; Anette Rickenlund; Maria J Eriksson; Nawzad Saleh; David Marlevi
abstract:
The primary mechanism of mitral regurgitation (MR) in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral leaflets due to septal hypertrophy narrowing the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT), influencing leaflet movement and closure. Among patients undergoing alcohol septal ablation (ASA), the impact on- and underlying mechanism of MR remains less studied. The aim was to determine the prevalence of MR and changes in MR severity after ASA and analyze echocardiographic (ECHO) parameters associated with MR changes.
All patients who underwent ASA at Karolinska University Hospital in Sweden, 2009-2021 (follow-up until 2025), were included in this retrospective cohort study. ECHO parameters were collected before ASA, at 1-year follow-up and at the latest follow-up registered. To evaluate differences in continuous values, Kruskal-Wallis test was used, and for categorical values, Fischer's exact test was used.
154 patients were included (mean follow-up 4.0 ± 3.9 years). 14% (n = 21) had at least moderate MR at baseline, of which 90% (n = 19) improved to mild MR or less. The patients with improved (n = 19, 12%) or unchanged (n = 128, 83%) grade of MR showed greater reduction of LVOT peak pressure gradients (improved MR: 137.5 to 4.8 mmHg, unchanged MR: 57.0 to 25.0 mmHg) between baseline and last follow-up, compared with patients with increased MR grade (n = 7, 4.5%, 57.0 to 51.0 mmHg, p = 0.003).
Among patients with at least moderate MR before ASA, MR severity generally improved at follow-up, potentially due to septal reduction and LVOT enlargement, which may have reduced SAM.
Not applicable.

title: Cellular senescence in calcific aortic valve disease: are we ready for senolytic therapy?
authors: Ludovica Simonini; Ilenia Foffa; Augusto Esposito; Cecilia Vecoli
abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is the most prevalent valvular heart disease in the Western countries and carries significant morbidity and mortality, yet no pharmacological therapy has demonstrated efficacy in modifying its natural history. Once regarded as a passive degenerative process, CAVD is now recognized as an actively regulated disease driven by endothelial dysfunction, chronic inflammation, dysregulated mineral metabolism, and cellular senescence, which collectively drive progressive fibrotic remodeling and calcification of the valve leaflets through both dystrophic and osteogenic mechanisms. This review examines the pharmacological strategies that have been investigated or are currently under evaluation to slow CAVD progression, encompassing lipid-lowering agents, renin-angiotensin system inhibitors, bone resorption inhibitors, vitamin K supplementation, and nitric oxide pathway modulators. Despite strong biological rationale and encouraging observational or preclinical data, each of these approaches has thus far failed to demonstrate consistent disease, modifying efficacy in prospective randomized trials, reflecting the complexity of CAVD pathophysiology and the historical lack of mechanistic precision in patient selection and trial design. Emerging evidence suggests that cellular senescence may represent a unifying and potentially actionable therapeutic target, bridging endothelial dysfunction, chronic inflammation, and active calcification within a single pathophysiological framework. Preclinical studies demonstrate that senolytic clearance of senescent cells reduces calcification in atherosclerosic and hypercholesterolemic vascular models provide a compelling rationale for extending this approach to valvular targets.

title: Concomitant Transcatheter Aortic and Tricuspid Valve Replacement.
authors: Jaiel Niamat; Claire Ren; Lucas Uchoa De Assis; Antigone Kostea; Jeroen Wilschut; Rutger-Jan Nuis
abstract:
Severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is associated with adverse outcomes.
A 65-year-old man with advanced right heart failure symptoms and torrential TR was accepted for transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR). After an unforeseen treatment delay, reassessment demonstrated progression of concomitant mild-to-moderate aortic stenosis (AS) to severe AS. He underwent successful TAVR and TTVR during 1 procedure with an excellent clinical outcome.
Given the sequence of disease progression with symptomatic torrential TR preceding the development of severe AS, an indication for TAVR and TTVR was established. A single-procedure strategy was favored over a staged approach based on the assumption that TAVR alone could increase forward flow and right-sided loading conditions, potentially worsening right heart failure.
Concomitant TAVR and TTVR may benefit selected patients. Pre-TAVR identification of patients requiring adjunctive TTVR and determination of the optimal timing (concomitant or staged) remain challenging.

title: Artificial Intelligence Detection of Aortic Valve Calcification on Routine Noncontrast Chest CT: A Real-World Cohort.
authors: Ofir Koren; Vivek Patel; Orit Wimpfheimer; Alexander Kukuev; Parker Chu; Harsh Jain; Kazuki Suruga; Hidemasa Shitan; Shiri Hassid; Daniel Ng; Shir Hofstetter; Raj R Makkar
abstract:
Routine noncontrast chest computed tomography (CT) may reveal aortic valve calcification (AVC) outside aortic stenosis evaluation. Its prevalence, burden, and documentation remain uncertain. Artificial intelligence (AI) may enable systematic detection.
The study aims to evaluate AVC prevalence and burden, clinical correlates, radiology documentation, and AI-assisted case finding.
This retrospective single-center study screened 511 consecutive noncontrast, non-electrocardiographically gated chest CT examinations in adults aged ≥50 years. After 15 protocol exclusions and 56 software-designated nonevaluable examinations, 440 underwent quantification by 2 blinded readers. AVC was defined as >10 AU using a 130-Hounsfield-unit threshold adjusted for blood-pool attenuation and image noise when needed. Locked HealthAVC V1.0 was a secondary comparator.
Manual quantification identified AVC in 172 of 440 scans (39.1%; 95% CI: 34.6%-43.7%); 97 of 440 (22.0%) had ≥100 AU. Inter-reader agreement at >10 AU was 99.5% (kappa = 0.990). Age (adjusted OR: 1.92 per 5 years; 95% CI: 1.63-2.26) and male sex (adjusted OR: 2.09; 95% CI: 1.32-3.30) were associated with AVC. Reports documented 27 of 172 positive scans (15.7%; 95% CI: 11.0%-21.9%). AI detected 169 of 172 manually confirmed cases (98.3%) among 440 evaluable scans, including 142 of 145 undocumented cases. Of 496 submitted scans, 56 (11.3%) were nonevaluable. End-to-end sensitivity counting positive rejected scans as missed was 89.9%. Among 86 AI-positive patients with echocardiography, 10 (11.6%) had mild-or-greater aortic stenosis.
AVC was common but infrequently documented on routine chest CT. AI detected most cases among evaluable scans; 11.3% were nonevaluable, yielding 89.9% end-to-end sensitivity. Prospective studies should assess clinical pathways.

title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Pure Aortic Regurgitation: The Randomized SEASON-AR Clinical Trial.
authors: Xiao-Fei Gao; Yan Wang; Hong Jiang; Bo Li; Yi-Bing Shao; Jun Luo; Fa-Xin Ren; Fan Ouyang; Zhi-Kui Chen; Hai-Tao Yuan; Cheng Wang; Bing Han; Ping-Xi Xiao; Yi-Qiang Yuan; Zhen-Wen Yang; Liu Miao; Xiang Ma; Jian Yang; Dong-Fang You; Shao-Liang Chen; Jun-Jie Zhang; SEASON-AR Trial Investigators
abstract:
For patients with severe pure aortic regurgitation (AR) at high surgical risk, guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) is often the only available option. Transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is an established treatment for aortic stenosis and has also been evaluated in patients with pure AR. However, no adequately powered randomized trial has compared TAVR with GDMT alone in this population.
We conducted a prospective, investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized, open-label trial in China. Patients with severe pure AR for whom surgery was considered difficult or unacceptable by the local heart team or who persistently declined surgery were randomly assigned at a 1:1 ratio to receive transfemoral TAVR with the VitaFlow system plus GDMT or GDMT alone. The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year.
We assigned 210 patients with severe pure AR to the TAVR group (n=109) or GDMT group (n=101) at 18 centers. At 1-year follow-up, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the primary end point was significantly lower in the TAVR group than in the GDMT group (8.3% vs 24.8%; hazard ration [HR], 0.31 [95% CI, 0.14-0.66]; P=0.001), driven primarily by a reduction in heart failure rehospitalization (3.7% vs 21.3%; HR, 0.16 [95% CI, 0.06-0.47]; P < 0.001). TAVR was associated with higher rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation, most of which occurred within 30 days after the procedure.
Among patients with severe pure AR, TAVR plus GDMT significantly reduced the rate of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year compared with GDMT alone despite higher 30-day rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation.

title: Mitochondrial Metabolism-Related Candidate Signatures in Calcific Aortic Valve Disease Spectrum: An Exploratory Integrative Bioinformatics Study.
authors: Min Yang; Yingjing Gui; Hongbo Qian; Dafa Zhang
abstract: ​Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is a progressive valvular disorder in which the role of mitochondrial metabolism remains incompletely understood. This exploratory study aimed to identify mitochondrial metabolism-related genes (MIMMRGs) associated with CAVD-spectrum valve remodeling. GSE83453 was used as the training dataset, and GSE51472 was used for expression-direction validation. Both datasets contain biologically and phenotypically heterogeneous groups of diseased valves. CAVD-associated differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were integrated with MIMMRGs, followed by functional enrichment analysis, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), and support vector machine-recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE), expression validation, immune infiltration analysis, transcription factor analysis, drug and compound prediction, and molecular docking. A total of 909 DEGs and 1,234 MIMMRGs were identified, yielding 67 candidate genes enriched in metabolic and biosynthetic processes. ACADL and TDO2 were identified as candidate biomarkers and exhibited consistent expression differences between CAVD and normal samples in both datasets. Gene set enrichment analysis indicated the involvement of chemokine-related and immune-regulatory pathways. Four immune cell types differed between the CAVD and normal groups, and ACADL and TDO2 exhibited opposite correlations with naive B cells. HNF4A, STAT3, and AR were predicted to be common transcriptional regulators. Molecular docking indicated favorable in silico interactions between doxorubicin and ACADL and between dexamethasone and TDO2. In conclusion, ACADL and TDO2 are candidate biomarkers associated with mitochondrial metabolism and immune-related processes in heterogeneous CAVD-spectrum valve lesions. These findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating and require independent clinical and experimental validation.

title: Paraparesis and left upper extremity weakness after total arch replacement with frozen elephant trunk: possible contributions of spinal cord ischaemia and cervical radiculopathy.
authors: Tomoaki Ishihama; Koki Yokawa; Yoshimitsu Shimatani; Kaede Uesugi; Ko Ishimoto; Tomonori Higuma; Kazunori Yoshida; Hidefumi Obo; Hidetaka Wakiyama
abstract: An 82-year-old man underwent total arch replacement with the frozen elephant trunk technique for an aortic arch aneurysm. Upon awakening 3 hours postoperatively, the patient exhibited flaccid paralysis of both lower extremities and left upper extremity weakness, whereas the right upper extremity was largely preserved. Cerebrospinal fluid drainage and blood pressure augmentation were initiated for suspected spinal cord ischemia. Lower-extremity motor function partially recovered, but left upper-extremity weakness persisted. Spinal magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated intramedullary T2 hyperintensity at T2/3 and bilateral neural foraminal stenosis from C3/4 to C6/7. Neurological examination revealed predominant weakness in the left C7 myotome with an absent left triceps reflexes, suggesting concomitant C7 radiculopathy. This case demonstrates that neurological deficits after aortic arch surgery may be multifactorial and highlights the value of detailed neurological examination and spinal imaging when upper extremity weakness is disproportionate.

title: Tissue Doppler S wave velocities are associated with changes in pro-brain natriuretic peptide levels following transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
authors: Sima Gharra; Gabby Elbaz-Greener; David Planer; Oren Yagel; David Leibowitz
journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
abstract:
Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is an effective treatment for severe aortic stenosis. Despite its efficacy, TAVI carries risks of complications in elderly patients. Prior research indicates that failure to reduce NTproBNP levels post-TAVI increases the risk of mortality and recurrent hospitalizations. The tissue Doppler S wave is an index of longitudinal left ventricular function which may predict poor outcomes following TAVI.
The aim of the study was to examine whether pre-TAVI S wave velocities are associated with hemodynamic response to TAVI as assessed by changes in NTproBNP levels.
This prospective observational study enrolled patients scheduled for elective TAVI who underwent echocardiographic evaluation including TDI S wave measurements. Blood levels of NTproBNP were assessed both before and 3 months after the procedure. Subjects were defined as responders or non-responders (NR) with response defined as a ≥ 30% reduction in NTproBNP levels post-procedure.
185 subjects (mean age 79 ± 9 yrs., 47% male) were included in the study. Response to TAVI was observed in 78 (42%) of the cohort. The NR group had a significantly higher incidence of hypertension (62.3% vs. 37.7%, P = 0.017). Median S wave was 6.96 (3.8-13.7) cm/s in the responders and 5.88 (3.77-12.1) cm/s in the NR (p = 0.001), a finding which remained significant on multivariate analysis (p = 0.004; OR 1.31 95%CI 1.09-1.59).
This study demonstrates that for the first time that the TDI S wave is a significant predictor of NTproBNP reduction following TAVI. Further research is needed to validate these results in larger populations.

title: Prognostic value of pre- and post-procedural TAPSE/PASP ratio for long-term mortality in patients with left ventricular ejection fraction < 50% undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
authors: Aysel Akhundova; Berhan Keskin; Umeyir Savur; Aykun Hakgor; Özlem Önder; Fatih E Olgun; Atakan Dursun; Hacı M Güneş; Beytullah Çakal; Bilal Boztosun
journal: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology
abstract:
Tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE)/pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP) ratio reflects right ventricular-pulmonary arterial (RV-PA) coupling and has prognostic value in heart failure and pulmonary hypertension. Its significance in patients with low ejection fraction (LVEF < 50%) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains unclear.
This study aimed to investigate the association between pre-procedural TAPSE/PASP ratio and long-term all-cause mortality and to determine whether post-TAVI TAPSE/PASP ratio assessed at discharge was associated with subsequent mortality in patients with severe AS and LVEF < 50%.
This single-center retrospective study included 225 consecutive patients with severe aortic stenosis and LVEF < 50% undergoing TAVI (2015-2025). TAPSE/PASP was measured at baseline and discharge. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality, analyzed using multivariable Cox regression.
Over a median follow-up of 1161 days, 102 (45.3%) patients died. Post-TAVI TAPSE/PASP was significantly higher in survivors (0.56 ±0.20 vs. 0.48 ±0.16 mm/mm Hg, p = 0.005) and was independently associated with long-term mortality (HR = 0.74 per 0.1 mm/mm Hg increase; 95% CI: 0.55-0.99; p = 0.04). Pre-TAVI TAPSE/PASP showed a borderline, non-significant association with mortality. Patients with post-TAVI TAPSE/PASP < 0.514 mm/mm Hg had significantly worse 5-year survival (log-rank p = 0.034).
In severe aortic stenosis with LVEF < 50%, post-TAVI TAPSE/PASP at discharge was independently associated with long-term mortality. The findings suggest that assessment of RV-PA coupling after TAVI may provide additional prognostic information, although the clinical utility of the proposed threshold requires prospective validation.

title: Changes in the institutional treatment of severe aortic stenosis following the introduction of transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
authors: Maja Rojko; Ema Kocjancic; Maja Kodra; Ales Pleskovic; Hrvoje Reschner; Matjaz Span; Nenad Danojevic; Miladin Ðordevic; Ninoslav Radovanovic; Metka Zorc; Stamenko Susak; Marko Noc
journal: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology
abstract:
Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has transformed the treatment of severe aortic stenosis.
To investigate the association of TAVI introduction on institutional volume and characteristics of patients treated for aortic stenosis either by surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) or TAVI.
A single-centre retrospective observational study of consecutive patients treated only with SAVR (SAVR-only period, 2004-2017) and with either SAVR or TAVI (SAVR + TAVI period, 2017-2025).
During the SAVR-only period, 1011 patients underwent SAVR, and during the SAVR + TAVI period, 685 patients underwent SAVR and 824 underwent TAVI. The total number of aortic valve interventions increased annually by 9% (95% CI: 1.08-1.10; p < 0.001), while SAVR decreased by 15% during the SAVR + TAVI period (95% CI: 0.82-0.89; p < 0.001). Cumulative 30-day mortality was 2.8% during the SAVR-only period and 1.5% during the SAVR + TAVI period (p = 0.021). Patients undergoing SAVR during the SAVR + TAVI period were younger (68 vs. 70 years; p < 0.001), had a lower Logistic EuroSCORE (4.52 vs. 6.33; p < 0.001) and less often underwent concomitant revascularization (29% vs. 35%; p = 0.013). Patients undergoing TAVI compared to SAVR were older (80 vs. 68 years; p < 0.001), had a higher Logistic EuroSCORE (11.39 vs. 4.52; p < 0.001), and had comparable 30-day mortality (1.0% vs. 2.0%; p = 0.083). The difference in 5-year mortality in favour of SAVR (13.8% vs. 27.4%) was not significant after adjustment for age, sex and Logistic EuroSCORE (HR = 0.794; 95% CI: 0.550-1.147; p = 0.22).
Introduction of TAVI was associated with increased institutional volume of aortic valve interventions despite a concomitant decrease in the number of SAVR procedures. TAVI appears to have expanded treatment to previously undertreated high-risk elderly patients while also being used in a sizable proportion of patients who previously underwent SAVR.

title: Prognostic value of preprocedural neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio for in-hospital and overall mortality in patients with reduced ejection fraction undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
authors: Kadir Biyikli; Mustafa Ferhat Keten; Nesri Danısman; Dogancan Ceneli; Can Erdem
journal: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology
abstract:
Patients with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) represent a particularly vulnerable subgroup with elevated perioperative and long-term mortality. The neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio (NPAR), an integrated marker of systemic inflammation and nutritional status, has not been specifically evaluated as a prognostic marker in this population.
To examine the prognostic value of preprocedural NPAR for in-hospital and overall (all-cause) mortality in patients with reduced LVEF undergoing TAVI.
This retrospective single-centre study enrolled 169 consecutive patients with severe aortic stenosis and LVEF < 50% undergoing TAVI between June 2020 and January 2026. Preprocedural NPAR was derived from blood samples obtained within 24 h before the procedure. In-hospital and overall mortality were assessed using logistic and Cox regression models with limited covariate adjustment.
Using an NPAR cut-off of 20.74, patients with elevated NPAR exhibited higher rates of chronic kidney disease, acute kidney injury, and both in-hospital and overall mortality, along with higher C-reactive protein and BNP levels and lower haemoglobin, albumin, postprocedural LVEF, and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE) values. NPAR remained associated with in-hospital mortality after adjustment for chronic kidney disease or TAPSE and was also associated with overall mortality in multivariable Cox regression analyses. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly reduced survival among patients with elevated NPAR.
After limited multivariable adjustment, preprocedural NPAR was associated with both in-hospital and overall mortality in patients with reduced LVEF undergoing TAVI. As a simple marker of inflammatory and nutritional burden, NPAR may provide additional prognostic information and complement preprocedural risk assessment, although its incremental value beyond established risk models and other biomarkers remains uncertain.

title: Outcomes After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Using the Self-Expanding Allegra Valve in Daily Practice.
authors: Justina Zemaite; Stefan Erler; Ulrich Schafer; Steffen Vormfelde; Bjoern Andrew Remppis; Katja Bohmann; Barbara Maria Januszewski; Christof Burgdorf
abstract:
Limited data are available of the self-expanding Allegra transcatheter heart valve (THV). The aim of this study was to investigate the safety and outcome of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) using the Allegra THV in daily practice.
Between February 2018 and September 2024, 142 consecutive patients underwent Allegra TAVI at the Heart and Vascular Center, Bad Bevensen, Germany, either for native aortic stenosis (AS) (n = 117, median 82 (interquartile range 80-86) years) or degenerated aortic bioprostheses (n = 25, 80 (73-84) years) as valve-in-valve (ViV) procedures. Endpoints were defined according to Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 criteria.
The logistic EuroSCORE II was significantly higher in the cohort of patients with degenerated aortic bioprostheses than in those with native AS (14.4% (6.6-25.3%) versus 3.3% (2.5-5.7%), P < 0.01). Technical success was nearly identical in both cohorts (91.5% of patients with native AS and 92.0% of patients with ViV TAVI). Postinterventional aortic regurgitation ≥ moderate was found in 4.5% of patients with native AS and was not present in any patient with ViV TAVI. In the native AS cohort, mean and maximal aortic pressure gradients decreased from 44 (36-54) mm Hg and 72 (60-87) mm Hg before the intervention to 6 (5-9) mm Hg and 12 (9-15) mm Hg after Allegra TAVI. In the ViV cohort, mean and maximal transvalvular pressure gradients decreased from 34 (27-43) mm Hg and 59 (44-70) mm Hg to 9 (7-11) mm Hg and 16 (14-23) mm Hg, respectively. Periprocedural mortality rates (≤ 30 days) were 6.8% and 12.0% in the native AS and ViV cohorts, respectively. One-year and 3-year survival rates were 87.2% and 73.2% in the native AS cohort and 89.8% and 75.1% in the ViV cohort, respectively.
TAVI using the self-expanding Allegra THV system is safe and leads to acute hemodynamic improvements in patients with native AS or degenerated aortic bioprostheses.

title: Changes in Long-Term Care Needs, Healthcare Costs, and Mortality Risk After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Japan: The Longevity Improvement & Fair Evidence Study.
authors: Toshiharu Sassa; Megumi Maeda; Futoshi Oda; Tomohiro Sakamoto; Haruhisa Fukuda
abstract:
Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is increasingly performed in older adults with severe aortic stenosis, but there is limited evidence on their post-procedure changes in care needs, healthcare costs, and mortality risk.
This retrospective cohort study used linked medical and long-term care (LTC) insurance claims data from 1361 patients aged ≥ 75 years who underwent TAVI in 13 Japanese municipalities. Patients were stratified into four groups by baseline certified care needs level: Independent (n = 725), Support Level 1-2 (n = 321), LTC Level 1-2 (n = 208), and LTC Level 3-5 (n = 107).
Among 532 patients in the 36-month observation cohort, 53% were independent at baseline, and approximately half of those remained independent at 36 months. Monthly total medical and LTC costs at 36 months were approximately 5 times higher in the LTC Level 3-5 group than the Independent group. The LTC Level 3-5 group also showed significantly higher all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 3.19, 95% confidence interval 2.18-4.67).
Higher baseline care needs are associated with poorer outcomes and higher costs after TAVI. Incorporating care needs levels into clinical assessments may inform clinical decision-making and resource planning in older populations.

title: Perioperative Care of Heart Failure, Arrhythmias, and Valvular Heart Disease.
authors: Avital Y O'Glasser; Efrén C Manjarrez
abstract: Frequently, the question of whether or not a patient is stable for surgery boils down to the question, "Does this patient need a preoperative stress test?" However, coronary artery disease and ischemic heart disease are only some of the many cardiac conditions that patients present with preoperatively-and that can negatively impact their intraoperative management and postoperative outcomes. This article will explore the evidence based, patient centered best practices surrounding the perioperative evaluation and management of heart failure, arrhythmias, and valvular heart disease.

title: Cat eye syndrome chromosome region, candidate 1 is a novel prognostic biomarker in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
authors: Yu Zhang; Fangfang Wan; Chen Li; Bo Wang; Mo Zhang; Minjie Lu; Lianming Kang; Liwen Liu; Jizheng Wang; Lei Song
abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) exhibits great prognostic heterogeneity, necessitating the identification of high-risk patients for timely treatment. This study aimed to find novel prognostic biomarkers directly from diseased cardiac tissue to improve risk stratification of HCM. We utilized a myocardial transcriptome discovery cohort (n = 246; median follow-up 6.8 years) alongside two independent plasma validation cohorts (Beijing, n = 1,238; follow-up 2.5 years; Xi'an, n = 402; follow-up 4.8 years). The primary and secondary endpoints were cardiovascular death and sudden cardiac death (SCD), respectively. In the discovery cohort, myocardial expression of CECR1 (cat eye syndrome chromosome region, candidate 1, also known as ADA2, Adenosine Deaminase 2) demonstrated the strongest association with cardiovascular death (P = 9.6 × 10-5). Plasma CECR1 levels correlated modestly but significantly with myocardial expression. In the Beijing validation cohort, decreased plasma CECR1 predicted increased risks of cardiovascular death (adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 3.731, P < 0.001) and SCD (adjusted HR 7.398, P < 0.001), with areas under the curves (AUCs) of 0.720 and 0.798, respectively. These findings were replicated in the Xi'an validation cohort. Integrating plasma CECR1 into the HCM Risk-SCD model significantly enhanced its predictive performance, increasing the AUC from 0.723 to 0.845 (P = 0.031) in the Beijing validation cohort and consistently improving it from 0.600 to 0.781 (P = 0.018) in the Xi'an validation cohort. In conclusion, CECR1 represents a novel prognostic biomarker of HCM. Measurement of CECR1 may improve risk stratification by facilitating the identification of individuals at higher risk of cardiovascular mortality. CECR1 assessment may provide additional information for SCD risk evaluation and support clinical decision-making regarding implantable cardioverter-defibrillator therapy.

title: Histologically Confirmed Myxedematous Myocardial Involvement in Severe Hypothyroidism With Concomitant Bicuspid Aortic Stenosis.
authors: Shubhang Sharma-Sharma; Jaime Galindo-Uribe; Sebastián Gutiérrez-Alanís; Aldo César Cázares-Diazleal; Zuilma Yurith Vásquez-Ortiz; Sandra Graciela Rosales-Uvera; Bernardo Pérez-Enríquez; Braulio Martínez-Benítez
abstract:
Histologically confirmed myxedematous myocardial involvement is rare and may be difficult to recognize when another cause of ventricular hypertrophy and fibrosis coexists.
A 40-year-old man with longstanding, inadequately treated primary hypothyroidism presented with exertional dyspnea and a large goiter. Echocardiography showed severe bicuspid aortic stenosis, moderate aortic regurgitation, marked concentric left ventricular hypertrophy, preserved ejection fraction, and severely reduced global longitudinal strain. Cardiac magnetic resonance demonstrated extensive late gadolinium enhancement involving approximately 26% of myocardial mass. After thyroid optimization, he underwent aortic valve replacement. Myocardial biopsy showed severe cardiomyocyte atrophy, interstitial mucin deposition, and extensive replacement fibrosis; Congo red staining was negative.
Severe aortic stenosis provided an alternative explanation for the myocardial phenotype, and multimodality imaging alone could not distinguish pressure-overload remodeling from hypothyroidism-related myocardial injury.
Histopathology established concomitant myxedematous myocardial involvement, highlighting the diagnostic value of tissue characterization in severe hypothyroidism.

title: Libman-Sacks Endocarditis as the First Presentation of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus in a Young Man: A Multisystemic Diagnostic Challenge.
authors: Scott Waring; Joseph W Fletcher; Aaron Jones
abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a complex, phenotypically varied disorder that possesses wide-ranging cardiac involvement. Libman-Sacks endocarditis (LSE) is one such cardiac manifestation, which results from the deposition of verrucous, sessile lesions favoring the left-sided heart valves. LSE is typically clinically silent without significant valvular dysfunction. Such patients with LSE, however, are those most susceptible to a more severe clinical phenotype resulting from SLE. Here, we report a unique case of a 22-year-old man initially presenting with unilateral leg swelling found to be secondary to a deep-vein thrombosis. He subsequently developed a constellation of acute symptoms, including embolic strokes, splenic infarction, proteinuric kidney injury, and significant mitral regurgitation, all of which mimicked bacterial endocarditis. His complex, multi-systemic disease course presented diagnostic challenges. We highlight the need in such complex cases for a specialist-led multidisciplinary approach, including cardiologists and rheumatologists, to guide serological and radiological investigations. Early use of echocardiography, in particular 3D transesophageal imaging, was paramount in clinching the diagnosis of LSE as an index presentation of SLE and in the transition from intravenous antibiotics to immunosuppression. Our case underscores the importance of the multidisciplinary team and the role of echocardiography in identifying such patients with LSE in SLE and thereby those most vulnerable to significant end-organ sequelae.
