title: Warfarin After Seven Decades: Persistent Value and the Contemporary Role of Vitamin K Antagonism.
authors: Weverton Ferreira Leite; Wilma Noia Ribeiro; Rui Manuel Dos Santos Povoa; Dirceu Rodrigues de Almeida; Daniela Fernanda Alli Hemerly; Braulio Luna Filho; Valdir Ambrosio Moises; Jose Antonio Franchini Ramires
abstract: Warfarin is one of the most enduring drugs in cardiovascular medicine. Although direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) have transformed anticoagulation, especially in atrial fibrillation (AF) eligible for DOAC therapy, their success cannot be extrapolated to every thrombotic substrate. This review examines the contemporary boundaries of warfarin and vitamin K antagonist (VKA) therapy. Mechanical heart valves remain the clearest setting in which lifelong international normalized ratio (INR)-guided VKA therapy is required; randomized attempts to substitute dabigatran or apixaban have failed. In rheumatic heart disease-associated AF, INVICTUS favored VKA therapy over rivaroxaban, supporting the VKA class rather than warfarin specifically. High-risk thrombotic antiphospholipid syndrome, particularly triple-positive disease, is another VKA-preferred setting. Left ventricular thrombus (LVT) occupies an evolving position in which warfarin remains established, while randomized evidence supports rivaroxaban as a potential alternative in selected acute post-myocardial infarction LVT. Pregnancy with mechanical valves requires dynamic maternal-fetal risk balancing, whereas advanced chronic kidney disease and dialysis represent areas of uncertainty rather than intrinsic indications for warfarin. The global relevance of warfarin also depends on total anticoagulation burden, including INR monitoring, travel, treatment continuity, quality of anticoagulation, and reversal capacity. The persistence of VKA efficacy in selected highly thrombogenic environments raises a biologically plausible hypothesis that broader suppression of vitamin K-dependent factors may matter, but this mechanism is not established by clinical trials. Contemporary anticoagulation should therefore be substrate-centered: VKA therapy remains necessary in some conditions, preferred in others, increasingly replaceable in several, and uncertain in a few.

title: Digoxin Revisited: An Updated Review in the Light of Recent Trials.
authors: Muhammad Saad; Muhammad Abdullah; Ankit Yelamarthy; Krystal John; Abbas Hayat Mallick; Behram Khan; Hassan Tahir; Rajan Krishnamani
abstract: Isolated from Digitalis species following William Withering's 1785 work on foxglove, digoxin inhibits myocardial Na+/K+-ATPase, raising intracellular calcium and vagal tone to produce inotropic, rate-controlling, and neurohormonal-deactivating effects. The foundational DIG trial (1997) showed no mortality benefit but reduced heart failure hospitalizations, prompting a progressive guideline downgrade. Three decades later, DIGIT-HF (2025, digitoxin) and DECISION (2026, low dose digoxin) retested cardiac glycosides atop modern four pillar guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT). DIGIT-HF significantly reduced the composite of death or worsening heart failure (hazard ratio (HR), 0.82), while DECISION showed a numerical but nonsignificant benefit. A pooled meta-analysis of DIG, DIGIT-HF, and DECISION (9,013 patients) confirmed a consistent 15% reduction in worsening heart failure events across three decades of changing background therapy, without a significant mortality effect. The Dig-RHD trial addressed an unstudied population: symptomatic rheumatic heart disease (RHD), a chronic valvular heart disease that results from permanent damage to cardiac valves due to group A streptococcal infection. RHD affects roughly 40 million people and causes approximately 300,000 deaths annually, disproportionately in low- and middle-income countries. In 1,769 patients randomized across 12 Indian centers, digoxin significantly reduced the composite of death or new-onset/worsening heart failure (31.4% vs. 35.5%; HR, 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.70 to 0.97; P = 0.02), with greater benefit in atrial fibrillation, women, and patients with low body mass index (BMI), and a number needed to treat of approximately 14 over 2 years. Digoxin is not a mortality-reducing drug, but pooled contemporary evidence establishes it as a reproducible, low-cost tool for reducing heart failure events, now supported for the first time by high-quality randomized data in RHD, a population with substantial global burden and no prior evidence-based medical therapy. These findings warrant reconsideration of digoxin's guideline status and development of RHD-specific recommendations.

title: Translational maturity of artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography varies across cardiovascular diseases.
authors: Huanhuan Chen; Jingjuan Huang; Xumin Hou
abstract: Electrocardiography is a widely available and low-cost cardiovascular test, and artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) can identify latent electrical phenotypes beyond conventional interpretation. However, high retrospective discrimination does not necessarily translate into clinically reliable or actionable benefit. This critical narrative review evaluates the translational maturity of AI-ECG across arrhythmias, acute myocardial infarction, heart failure, valvular heart disease, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and cardiac amyloidosis. PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Web of Science were searched from January 1, 2022, through July 10, 2026, with earlier landmark studies added by backward citation tracking. Seventy-seven publications informed the review. Evidence was appraised using five clinically oriented criteria: intended use, reference-standard reliability, external validation and transportability, clinical actionability, and effects on workflow or patient outcomes. AI-ECG has progressed furthest in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction triage and reduced-left-ventricular-ejection-fraction screening, where prospective or randomized studies have demonstrated workflow or diagnostic-yield benefits, whereas acute myocardial infarction rule-out has reached prospective multicenter diagnostic validation. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy screening has also advanced through international validation and prospective implementation. By contrast, occlusion myocardial infarction detection, prediction of occult or future atrial fibrillation, valvular heart disease, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, long-term heart-failure prediction, and cardiac amyloidosis remain primarily validation-stage or risk-enrichment applications. Across domains, broader adoption is constrained by label quality, calibration, transportability, operating-threshold selection, and limited patient-outcome evidence. AI-ECG is therefore best positioned as clinician-supervised decision support linked to explicit downstream testing and care pathways.

title: Regional Divergence in Infective Endocarditis Prophylaxis: A Multi-center Analysis of Clinical Practice vs. International Guidelines from the Pan Arab Congenital Heart Disease Association (PACHDA).
authors: Ali Al Akhfash; Nagib Dahdah; Milad El-Segaier
abstract: Current infective endocarditis (IE) prophylaxis guidelines recommend a restrictive approach, excluding low-risk lesions such as patent ductus arteriosus, isolated ventricular septal defect, and valvular stenosis. In many countries, delayed cardiac defect repair and a high prevalence of dental disease may create a distinct risk profile that warrants further investigation. The Pan Arab Congenital Heart Disease Association (PACHDA) conducted a multinational cross-sectional online survey targeting cardiovascular specialists to evaluate perceptions of IE prophylaxis guidelines, adherence patterns, and the influence of oral health and socioeconomic factors on clinical decision-making. Statistical analyses included Spearman rank correlation, Chi-square testing, Fisher's exact test, and qualitative thematic synthesis. The questionnaire was completed by 72 specialists, of whom only 25% reported strict adherence to restrictive international guidelines for isolated simple congenital heart defects. Respondents who identified socioeconomic barriers (e.g., poverty and limited access to dental care) as a primary concern were more likely to deviate from restrictive guideline recommendations than their peers (83.7% vs. 41.4%; p = 0.001). Clinicians with higher IE case exposure (> 5 IE cases in the preceding 5 years) also demonstrated significantly greater rates of guideline deviation (p = 0.047). Fewer than 50% of respondents considered current AHA/ESC guidelines "fit for purpose" in their local practice. Many cardiovascular specialists across the Arab/MENA region perceive current international IE prophylaxis recommendations as insufficiently reflective of local clinical and socioeconomic realities. However, these findings represent clinician perceptions and practice patterns rather than patient-level outcomes and should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating. The observed divergence between guideline recommendations and clinical practice highlights the need for regional epidemiological and outcome-based studies to determine whether local factors influence IE risk and whether adaptation of current prophylaxis strategies is warranted.

title: Remodeling of Failed Pulmonary Valve Autografts After the Ross Procedure.
authors: Vaclav Stejskal; Tereza Sokolova; Jakub Sagat; Barbora Vasova; Lucia Hrnciarova; Petr Smolak
abstract: The Ross procedure utilizes a pulmonary autograft for aortic valve replacement, but late autograft failure remains a clinical challenge. In this exploratory study, we characterized structural alterations in failed pulmonary autografts using digital morphometric analysis. Five autografts explanted because of regurgitation were compared with six autopsy control pulmonary valves using special stains and alpha-smooth muscle actin immunohistochemistry. One histologically most affected section per valve was evaluated using QuPath. Failed autografts showed leaflet thickening, elastosis, fibrosis, and myxomatous matrix accumulation. Compared with controls, autografts had greater maximum leaflet thickness (1.540 vs. 0.447 mm; P = 0.004), cross-sectional area (8.730 vs. 3.045 mm²; P = 0.004), α-SMA-positive area (0.707 vs. 0.046 mm²; P = 0.008), and α-SMA-positive area fraction (0.069 vs. 0.016; P = 0.017). The findings demonstrate extracellular matrix alterations and increased α-SMA immunoreactivity in hotspot regions, suggesting a myxomatous-like remodeling pattern.

title: Outcomes of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in the Middle East and North Africa: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Mohammad-Mahdi Bastan; Sahand Siami; Fatemeh Jodeiri; Sina Kazemian; Mandana Ebrahimzade; Niloofar Seighali; Saba Maleki; Nazanin Anaraki; Magdy Abdelhamid; Saif-El-Dean Abdel-Rahman; Kaveh Hosseini
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
abstract:
Data on transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) outcomes in the Middle East and North Africa region are limited. We synthesized available evidence on post-TAVR clinical outcomes in the Middle East and North Africa region.
We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Scopus from inception through May 2025 for studies reporting TAVR outcomes in this region. Outcomes included device success, all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, new-onset atrial fibrillation, moderate to severe paravalvular leak, and permanent pacemaker implantation. Overall incidence rates were pooled via Poisson analysis and reported per 100 person-years with 95% CIs.
Forty-eight studies encompassing 7331 patients (mean age, 76.9±8.5 years; 52.4% women) were included. Pooled device success rate was 96.4% (95% CI, 95.8%-97.0%). At latest follow-up, pooled incidence rates per 100 person-years were 13.7 for all-cause death (95% CI, 12.9-14.6), 4.8 for cardiovascular death (95% CI, 4.1-5.7), 1.0 for myocardial infarction (95% CI, 0.7-1.4), 1.6 for stroke (95% CI, 1.3-1.9), 2.7 for moderate to severe paravalvular leak (95% CI, 2.2-3.4), 6.5 for new-onset atrial fibrillation (95% CI, 5.5-7.7), and 10.0 for permanent pacemaker implantation (95% CI, 9.2-10.9). Post hoc exploratory meta-regression identified significant study-level modifying effects, with higher mean age and greater use of first-generation versus second-generation valves associated with higher overall all-cause mortality incidence following TAVR. Certainty of evidence was low or very low across all outcomes.
TAVR in the Middle East and North Africa region was associated with high device success rate and relatively low cardiovascular death. Permanent pacemaker implantation was the most prevalent post-TAVR complication. Further studies are warranted to optimize TAVR practice in this region.

title: Comparison of 1-year costs of commercially insured patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing surgical vs. transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
authors: Suzanne J Baron; Benjamin Z Galper; Marcella A Kelley; Soumya G Chikermane; Shannon M E Murphy
abstract:
Patients with aortic stenosis (AS) have been shown to have lower costs at 1 year with transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) compared with surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) in a Medicare population. The difference in costs between TAVR and SAVR in commercially insured patients with AS in the United States is unknown.
Using the Optum claims database, AS patients receiving either TAVR or SAVR between 3/2019 and 9/2022 were identified. Patients were categorized into low, intermediate or high strata using the Hospital Frailty Risk Score (HFRS). The primary outcome was total 1-year cost, defined as the sum of index AVR hospitalization and 1-year follow-up costs. Risk-adjusted generalized linear models were used to assess the difference in the costs between TAVR and SAVR.
3,623 patients (952 TAVR; 2,671 SAVR) were identified. TAVR patients had lower index hospitalization costs compared with SAVR patients across all HFRS strata (cost difference for low: $39,312, p < 0.01; intermediate: $42,006, p < 0.01; high: $39,431, p = 0.03). Cumulative costs through one year were significantly lower with TAVR in the low and intermediate HFRS strata (cost difference for low: $32,116, p < 0.01; intermediate $40,905, p < 0.01) and numerically lower in the high HFRS stratum (cost difference: $35,881, p = 0.15). When the analysis was restricted to isolated AVR, the 1-year difference was no longer significant in the low and intermediate HFRS strata ($8,064 and $11,314, respectively) and was numerically reversed in the high HFRS stratum (-$28,804).
In a commercial payor population of real-world patients with AS, TAVR was associated with lower standardized index hospitalization costs across all HFRS strata and lower standardized 1-year costs in the low and intermediate HFRS strata. These findings demonstrate that baseline frailty and procedural scope are critical determinants of short and intermediate-term cost differences between TAVR and SAVR for the treatment of AS in commercial populations.

title: Clustering of Cardiovascular Risk Factors in Midlife Forms Trajectories That Affect Heart Aging Biomarker and Incidence of Cardiovascular Disease.
authors: Arya Panthalanickal Vijayakumar; Tom Wilsgaard; Henrik Schirmer; Haakon Lindekleiv; Zachi I Attia; Francisco Lopez-Jimenez; David A Leon; Olena Iakunchykova
abstract:
To (1) identify multivariable longitudinal midlife patterns of systolic and diastolic blood pressure, body mass index, and non-high density lipoprotein cholesterol and (2) assess whether electrocardiogram derived heart age acceleration (δ-age) mediates their associations with incident myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, and all-cause mortality.
We analyzed 5244 participants from the observational cohort study, the Tromsø Study, who were free of MI or stroke at baseline (Tromsø7, 2015-2016) and attended at least 3 surveys (Tromsø3-7, 1986-2016). Age-standardized risk factor z-scores were modeled with quadratic B-splines and grouped using K-means clustering to identify joint multivariable life-course risk profiles. δ-Age was derived from 12-lead electrocardiograms using a validated neural network. Natural-effects models decomposed hazard ratios between clusters and clinical events (follow-up to 2021) into direct and δ-age mediated components.
Four distinct clusters were identified: stable low-risk (cluster 1, n=1604, 30.6%), dyslipidemia (cluster 2, n=1340, 25.6%), hypertension (cluster 3, n=1476, 28.1%), and high-risk trajectory (cluster 4, n=824, 15.7%). Each 1-SD increment in δ-age was associated with 27% to 30% of excess MI, stroke, and death, independent of age and sex. Clusters 3 and 4 carried the greatest excess risk of clinical events, whereas mediation by δ-age was modest (4%-8% of total effect for MI and stroke) and not statistically significant.
Joint multivariable life-course clustering of conventional risk factors identified clinically distinct long-term cardiovascular risk phenotypes. Although δ-age adds independent prognostic information, it explained little of the excess risk associated with chronic hypertension, dyslipidemia, or obesity, indicating it functions primarily as a parallel marker and not a causal mediator.

title: The association of left atrial volume index and coronary artery disease in type 2 diabetic patients without a history of hypertension and valvular heart disease.
authors: Mohammad Parsa Mahjoob; Roxana Sadeghi; Mohammad Haji Aghajani; Fatemeh Omidi; Mostafa Rostamnezhad; Mohadese Salehi
abstract:
Left atrial volume index (LAVI) evaluated using echocardiography serves a powerful predictor of cardiovascular outcomes. Since type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a main risk factor for coronary artery disease (CAD), the present investigation was conducted to examine the association between LAVI and incidence of CAD in diabetic patients.
In this case-control study, 90 type 2 diabetic patients aged 18-70 years who underwent coronary angiography at Imam Hossein Hospital, Tehran, between 2023 and 2024 were consecutively enrolled. Patients with hypertension, valvular heart disease, heart failure, or respiratory diseases were excluded. Cases (n = 45) had coronary artery disease (≥ 50% stenosis on angiography), while controls (n = 45) had no significant stenosis. Left atrial volume index (LAVI) was measured by echocardiography and classified as abnormal if ≥ 34 mL/m². All variables including LAVI were compared between two groups. Multivariate logistic regression was performed to investigate the role of variables in predicting CAD incidence in diabetic patients.
A total of 90 patients with type 2 diabetes were included (45 with CAD and 45 without CAD); the mean age was 51.48±5.68 years, and 60% were male. Analyses revealed that LAVI values were significantly higher in patients with CAD compared to those without (P = 0.018), while there were no significant differences between two groups regarding gender, age, smoking, insulin dependence, diabetes duration, HbA1c, FBS, EF. also, no significant differences were observed in other echocardiographic measures including mild LVH, mild diastolic dysfunction, heart rate. Multivariate logistic regression identified LAVI as an independent predictor of CAD (OR = 1.24; 95% CI: 1.06-1.45), P = 0.006. ROC curve analysis showed that a LAVI cut-off of 28 mL/m² predicted CAD with 71% sensitivity and 51% specificity (P = 0.016).
LAVI could be a potentially useful, accessible and practical index for screening CAD in diabetic patients. It may be proposed as part of the workup for the diagnosis and management of CAD in type 2 diabetic patients.

title: Evolving practices in pretransplant cardiovascular screening: moving toward personalized assessments.
authors: Arzu Velioglu; Tansu Celik; Harun Coban; Dilek Barutcu Atas; Altug Cincin; Serhan Tuglular
abstract: Cardiovascular (CV) disease remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with end-stage kidney disease, including those evaluated for kidney transplantation. Pretransplant CV screening has traditionally focused on detecting occult coronary artery disease and guiding revascularization to reduce perioperative risk. However, emerging evidence, most notably from the ISCHEMIA-CKD trial, has challenged this paradigm, demonstrating no clear benefit of routine invasive strategies or prophylactic revascularization in stable, asymptomatic patients over optimal medical therapy. Risk assessment in kidney transplant candidates should rely on an integrated clinical evaluation that incorporates symptoms, functional capacity, baseline electrocardiography and echocardiographic findings, and the presence of major CV risk factors. When further evaluation is indicated, stress echocardiography is generally preferred as the noninvasive modality. Invasive coronary angiography should be reserved for patients with cardiac symptoms or findings suggestive of significant ischemia, including reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, regional wall motion abnormalities, or moderate-to-large ischemia on stress testing. Pre-emptive revascularization should be limited to established guideline-based indications, such as left main disease, multivessel disease with reduced ejection fraction, or refractory angina despite optimal medical therapy. Noncoronary CV disorders, including heart failure, valvular disease, and pulmonary hypertension, require systematic assessment and cardiology referral. In conclusion, pretransplant CV assessment is shifting from protocol-driven screening toward individualized, clinical suspicion-based evaluation, prioritizing optimal medical therapy, avoidance of unnecessary testing, and timely access to transplantation.

title: Coxiella burnetii infective endocarditis involving a valved right ventricle-to-pulmonary artery conduit after Rastelli repair in an adolescent: a case report.
authors: Zonghui Hou; Junxiang Pan; Feiyang Wang; Mengqi Zhao; Xuechen Liu; Lianyi Wang
abstract:
Coxiella burnetii is an important cause of blood culture-negative infective endocarditis (IE). Pediatric C. burnetii endocarditis is rare, particularly in patients with prosthetic cardiovascular materials.
A 13-year-old boy with pulmonary atresia who had undergone Rastelli repair followed by replacement with a valved right ventricle-to-pulmonary artery (RV-PA) conduit presented with recurrent fever and a mobile intraconduit mass. Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) showed a vegetation in the pulmonary valve/conduit region, and cardiac computed tomography (CT) confirmed a corresponding filling defect without periconduit abscess or pseudoaneurysm. Blood metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) detected C. burnetii, while indirect immunofluorescence assay (IFA) showed positive phase I and phase II IgG antibodies. The conduit vegetation and blood detection of C. burnetii fulfilled major imaging and microbiological criteria, respectively, under the 2023 Duke-International Society for Cardiovascular Infectious Diseases criteria. An individualized regimen of doxycycline, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX), and hydroxychloroquine was followed by clinical improvement and reduction in lesion size during hospitalization.
C. burnetii should be considered in children with prosthetic cardiovascular materials who present with persistent fever and negative conventional blood cultures. Molecular testing, serology, and multimodality cardiac imaging can support diagnosis and early follow-up.

title: Code-Free Automated Machine-Learning (AutoML) Classification of Curated MRI Images Labeled for Rare Neurological Diseases: An Image-Level Proof-of-Concept Study.
authors: Mark A Bachir; Neel Nawathey; Alexander Bachir; Akshay J Reddy; Jasmeen K Cheema; Rakesh Patel
abstract: Rare neurological disorders present substantial diagnostic and research challenges because their low prevalence limits clinical exposure and the availability of large, well-characterized imaging datasets. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) plays an important role in many of these disorders because developmental, vascular, and neurodegenerative abnormalities may produce recognizable imaging phenotypes. Although deep-learning methods have demonstrated substantial potential for medical image analysis, conventional model development commonly requires programming expertise, computational infrastructure, and specialized knowledge of neural-network design. This image-level proof-of-concept study evaluated whether a commercially available code-free automated machine-learning (AutoML) platform could classify curated Joint Photographic Experts Group (JPEG) brain MRI images according to five inherited rare neurological disease labels. The individual image, rather than the patient or MRI examination, was the unit of analysis, and the supplied labels were not independently clinically adjudicated. A publicly available Kaggle dataset initially contained 2,000 images distributed equally among Walker-Warburg syndrome (WWS), pachygyria with cerebellar hypoplasia, Moyamoya disease, pantothenate kinase-associated neurodegeneration (PKAN; labeled as Hallervorden-Spatz disease in the source dataset), and Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy (FCMD). Exact-file hash analysis identified 12 duplicate image contents, leaving 1,988 unique files. This procedure removed exact binary duplicates but could not identify adjacent slices, transformed or near-duplicate images, or multiple images from the same patient or examination. Google Cloud Vertex AI (Google LLC, Mountain View, CA, USA) AutoML randomly assigned 1,588 images (79.9%) to training, 200 (10.1%) to validation, and 200 (10.1%) to testing. A single-label multiclass classifier was trained using a maximum budget of eight node-hours. The model achieved an overall micro-averaged area under the precision-recall curve (AuPRC) (average precision) of 1.000, with overall precision and recall of 100% at a confidence threshold of 0.50. Each label contributed 40 test images, and all 40 in each class were correctly classified, corresponding to a class-specific correct-classification proportion of 100% (exact 95% CI, 91.2%-100.0%). Across the complete test set, 200/200 images were correctly classified, corresponding to an observed image-level accuracy of 100% (exact 95% CI, 98.2%-100.0%). These findings demonstrate workflow feasibility and separability of the supplied image labels within this curated benchmark. However, patient- and examination-level independence could not be established; the effective independent sample size may be smaller than the nominal image count, and dataset-specific technical characteristics or shortcut learning may have contributed to the observed performance. These results should not be interpreted as evidence of patient-level diagnostic accuracy, clinical robustness, or generalizability. Independent patient-level and multicenter validation using clinically representative MRI examinations is required before diagnostic relevance can be established.

title: RadTex: Learning Efficient Radiograph Representations from Text Reports.
authors: Keegan Quigley; Miriam Cha; Ruizhi Liao; Geeticka Chauhan; Steven Horng; Seth Berkowitz; Polina Golland
journal: Resource-efficient medical image analysis : first MICCAI Workshop, REMIA 2022, Singapore, September 22, 2022, Proceedings. REMIA (Workshop) (1st : 2022 : Singapore ; Online)
abstract: Automated analysis of chest radiography using deep learning has tremendous potential to enhance the clinical diagnosis of diseases in patients. However, deep learning models typically require large amounts of annotated data to achieve high performance - often an obstacle to medical domain adaptation. In this paper, we build a data-efficient learning framework that utilizes radiology reports to improve medical image classification performance with limited labeled data (fewer than 1000 examples). Specifically, we examine image-captioning pretraining to learn high-quality medical image representations that train on fewer examples. Following joint pretraining of a convolutional encoder and transformer decoder, we transfer the learned encoder to various classification tasks. Averaged over 9 pathologies, we find that our model achieves higher classification performance than ImageNet-supervised and in-domain supervised pretraining when labeled training data is limited.

title: Masked Generative Distillation for Robust Multi-Lead-to-Single-Lead ECG Classification on IoMT Devices.
authors: Anandu Shivakumar; Obada Al-Khatib; Ghalia Nassreddine; Abeer ElKhouly
abstract: Wearable Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices typically rely on single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) acquisition, which supports ambulatory monitoring but provides less spatial information than 12-lead clinical ECG and is more susceptible to signal corruption. Deploying accurate deep learning models on wearable hardware is also constrained by limited memory, computation and energy. This study investigates whether diagnostic knowledge from a multi-lead ECG model can be transferred to a lightweight single-lead model while improving robustness under wearable-relevant noise. A teacher-student framework is proposed in which a 12-lead 1D ResNet-18 teacher transfers knowledge to a compact single-lead convolutional neural network using masked generative distillation (MGD). The framework is evaluated on PTB-XL through a controlled ablation study covering supervised learning, conventional knowledge distillation, MGD and noise augmentation. All student variants achieve comparable macro F1 performance on clean data, indicating that the main benefit lies in robustness rather than clean-condition classification. Combining MGD with noise augmentation provides the strongest robustness under synthetic noise. Simulation-based profiling demonstrates a 45-fold parameter reduction, lower inference latency and minimal performance change after INT8 quantization. On the PTB-XL five-superclass task, the model achieves a macro F1-score of 0.6449 versus 0.626 for MVKT-ECG, although differences in lead selection and evaluation protocols prevent strict comparison.

title: A multi-task deep learning-based approach to identify and assess dry root rot disease in chickpea.
authors: Piyush Priya; Joe Johnson; Athimoolam Durgadevi; Navaneeth Vinayachandran; Meghna Pillai; Bharat Maitraya; Muthukumar V Bagavathiannan; Muthappa Senthil-Kumar
abstract:
Dry root rot (DRR), an emerging global disease exacerbated by drought, affects a wide range of crops. The disease symptoms are manually scored for large-scale germplasm screening to identify disease-resistant varieties and test transgenic lines and other varieties. Despite its use in the past, manual disease identification is not only cumbersome but also often incapable of distinguishing between similar stress phenotypes. Manual disease scoring is tedious, time-consuming, and often error-prone, especially when screening large numbers of plants. To overcome this limitation, we developed a machine learning model that employs a learning-based approach using convolutional neural networks for automated feature extraction and image-based identification and severity assessment of DRR.
Our models were trained, tested, and validated using an in-house dataset of 10,800 unique RGB images. A total of 51 deep learning models, including single-task and multi-task models, were developed using the Xception and Vision Transformer (ViT) architectures with standard image augmentations, and then validated on stratified independent test sets to demonstrate robustness across camera, scanner, and microscope modalities.
The best multi-task ViT model, capable of scoring across combined datasets, achieved 94% accuracy in distinguishing DRR from the control and had a root mean square error of 1 in predicting DRR severity score.
This model's metrics, including confusion matrix performance, underscore its potential as an efficient and accessible tool for large-scale germplasm screening for DRR, overcoming the challenges of manual scoring.

title: Students' Perceptions of Online Learning and their Correlations with Deep Learning and Proactive Decision-making in Higher Education.
authors: Venny Rosalina; Yenni Rozimela; Indrayuda Indrayuda; Fabio Yuda; Erwin Mardiansyah
abstract: Online learning increases student flexibility and engagement, but its effectiveness depends on a design that encourages deep learning and proactive decision-making rather than just surface activities. This study aims to examine the relationships among student perceptions of online learning, deep learning tendencies, and proactive decision-making abilities in 202 students (M ± SD = 20.46 ± 1.75). Data were collected using the Distance Education Learning Environments Survey (DELES), the Revised Two Factor Study Process Questionnaire (R-SPQ-2F), and the Students' Proactive Decision-Making Scale (SPDMS-18). Spearman's test showed that positive perceptions of online learning were significantly related to deep learning (ρ = 0.634, p < 0.001) and proactive decision-making (ρ = 0.474, p < 0.001). Descriptive results showed a positive trend in all online learning indicators, fluctuations in motivation and deep learning strategies in the middle semester, and high stability in the proactive decision-making aspect. These findings confirm that high-quality online learning experiences encourage the adoption of deep learning approaches and proactive decision-making, including intrinsic motivation, analytical strategies, initiative, and goal-setting. Practical implications emphasize the importance of digital pedagogy training for lecturers, the development of e-learning systems that support student independence, and curricula that stimulate analysis and reflection. This research contributes to the design of digital-based higher education oriented toward 21st-century competencies.

title: A CT Lesion Foundation Model for Non-Invasive Assessment of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Aggressiveness and Prediction of Recurrence Risk.
authors: Wei Xia; Zhehan Shen; Mengsi Li; Jianxin Lu; Ji Xia; Yang Cheng; Wenzheng Li; Shunjie Dong; Lin Deng; Ruokun Li
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with high recurrence rates following curative resection. Accurate non-invasive assessment of tumor aggressiveness and recurrence risk is critical for surgical decision-making and postoperative surveillance, yet remains challenging with conventional imaging modalities. Here, we developed a CT lesion foundation model (LFM), trained via self-supervised learning on 32,120 generic lesion and 6,387 HCC-specific CT patches to capture transferable intra-lesional imaging phenotypes. Across one internal and two external validation cohorts, the sequentially pretrained LFM (LFM-Seq) achieved area under the curve values of 0.916, 0.846, and 0.920 for microvascular invasion (MVI) assessment, and 0.833, 0.885 and 0.795 for pathological grade assessment. The model remained robust under scenarios of limited training data and tumor localization perturbations. Furthermore, LFM-Seq-derived risk scores stratified recurrence-free survival (RFS), yielding an externally validated C-index of 0.701, and remained independently associated with RFS after adjusting for clinicopathological factors. Exploratory biological interpretability analyses showed that LFM-Seq-derived risk phenotypes were associated with suppressed lymphocyte-related immune programs. These results suggest that CT lesion foundation models can support non-invasive and robust characterization of HCC aggressiveness, recurrence risk stratification and discovery of interpretable prognostic imaging biomarkers.

title: Non-Invasive Assessment of Perineural Invasion Density: A Novel Marker for Prognosis and Treatment Stratification in Prostate Cancer.
authors: Bohao Liu; Long Zhang; Weian Zhu; Meng Yang; Xiang Liu; Xiaoyang Li; Peng Qin; Zhengxu Lin; Qian Cai; Jiayu Zheng; Xiao Zhao; Chen Zou; Xuan Wen; Longhao Xu; Daqin Wu; Lin Zhang; Cuilian Zhang; Kaiwen Li; Chunhui Wang; Wenlong Zhong; Yun Luo
abstract: We established and validated perineural invasion density (PNID) as a superior prognostic marker and developed an MRI-based AI model for its preoperative prediction. In this multicenter study of 1091 PCa patients undergoing radical prostatectomy, we evaluated PNID's association with biochemical recurrence (BCR) and radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS). We also analyzed concurrent β-blocker or antimuscarinic use with adjuvant ADT. A deep learning model was developed in a primary cohort (n = 523) and validated in two external cohorts (n = 317, 251). High-PNID was an independent prognostic factor for BCR (HR 4.06, 95% CI: 2.75-5.97, P < 0.001) and rPFS (HR 4.61, 95% CI: 2.97-7.16, P < 0.001). Notably, concurrent β-blocker use was significantly associated with favorable BCR outcomes exclusively in the High-PNID subgroup (HR 0.32, 95% CI: 0.12-0.84, P = 0.021), with no benefit in the Non-High PNID population or with antimuscarinics. The AI model showed excellent performance predicting High-PNID, with AUCs of 0.917 (training), 0.842 (internal validation), 0.889 and 0.915 (external validations). Model-identified High-PNID patients had significantly worse outcomes. PNID surpasses traditional PNI in prognostic accuracy and identifies a high-risk phenotype. High-PNID may define a subgroup benefiting from adjuvant β-blocker therapy, providing an exploratory clinical rationale for targeting the nerve-tumor microenvironment in stratified subpopulations. Hence, this model may be a reliable, non-invasive tool for preoperative identification of this high-risk subgroup, aiding clinicians in personalized risk stratification and treatment planning.

title: Lobar analysis of classical and deep learning radiomic features in chronic airflow limitation.
authors: Emelie Bäcklin; Birgitta Janerot-Sjoberg; Örjan Smedby; Magnus Sköld; Eva Breznik
abstract:
Quantitative chest computed tomography (CT) enables detailed assessment of structural lung abnormalities in chronic airflow limitation (CAL). We evaluated whether lobe-based classical radiomics and frozen deep learning transfer features from inspiratory and expiratory CT improved discrimination of CAL compared with handcrafted quantitative measures.
In this population-based study, 2,579 participants underwent inspiratory and expiratory CT and post-bronchodilator spirometry. CAL, defined as post-bronchodilator FEV₁/FVC < 0.70, was the primary modeling endpoint and was present in 430 participants; 2,149 participants without CAL served as controls. Lung lobes were segmented using nnU-Net. Classical radiomic features were extracted with PyRadiomics, and deep learning transfer features were obtained from frozen 3D U-Net and SegResNet encoders pretrained on the non-lung AbdomenAtlas dataset. A previously developed handcrafted feature set was included as a reference. Elastic-net regularized logistic regression with 10-fold cross-validation was used for classification, and performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).
Models based on expiratory features outperformed inspiratory-only models (AUC improvement 0.03-0.08). The best performance was achieved by classical radiomics combining inspiratory and expiratory features (AUC 0.87; positive predictive value 49%; negative predictive value 95%), exceeding the handcrafted model (AUC 0.81; PPV 34%; NPV 94%). Frozen transfer features from the non-lung-pretrained encoders showed slightly lower discrimination than classical radiomics, and combining feature types did not improve performance.
Lobe-based classical radiomics from combined inspiratory and expiratory CT improved cross-validated discrimination of spirometry-defined CAL in this population-based cohort, with expiratory imaging contributing substantially to optimal performance.

title: ESMRank: learning-to-rank prediction of missense variant effects from deep mutational scanning data.
authors: Riccardo Arnese; Gennaro Gambardella
abstract: Predicting the functional effects of missense variants is limited both by predictor performance and by the lack of principled strategies to integrate heterogeneous multiplexed assays of variant effect (MAVEs), including deep mutational scanning, into transferable sequence-function models. Here, we show that redundancy among partially overlapping deep mutational scanning experiments, often treated as noise, yields a consensus landscape of mutational constraint. We introduce "variant soundness", an overlap-aware rank-fusion score that uses cross-experiment consistency to derive an assay-agnostic ordering of mutational tolerance within proteins. Applied to ~1100 MAVEs spanning over two million missense variants, this approach reveals a mutational landscape enriched for structural stability constraints. Guided by this integrated signal, we develop ESMRank, a sequence-based learning-to-rank predictor combining ESM2 representations with physicochemical descriptors. Under strict protein-level partitioning, ESMRank outperforms widely used predictors across abundance-, folding-, and stability-related assays in ProteinGym and Domainome. Predicted deleterious variants are enriched for ClinVar pathogenicity and, in CFTR, correlate with folding efficiency, channel activity, and pharmacological responsiveness. Together, these results turn assay redundancy into a scalable resource for interpretable missense variant prediction.

title: Predicting persistent fever in patients with cancer receiving antibiotics: a machine learning approach.
authors: Gernot Pucher; Sanjat Kanjilal; Kevin Kopp; Aman Deep; Till Rostalski; Martin Schuler; Felix Nensa; Jens Kleesiek; H Christian Reinhardt; Christopher M Sauer
abstract: Persistent fever after initiating intravenous antibiotics is common in hospitalized patients with cancer and often leads to additional imaging and antimicrobial escalation. Early identification of patients unlikely to remain febrile could provide additional information during clinical reassessment. We developed and externally validated machine learning models to predict persistent fever 48-72 h after antibiotic initiation using electronic health records from two academic hospitals. Adult cancer patients with fever within 24-48 h of treatment were included. Models incorporated demographics, comorbidities, laboratory results, vital signs, and temperature patterns. The best-performing model achieved an AUROC of 0.82 (95% CI 0.79-0.84) internally and 0.78 (95% CI 0.77-0.79) externally. Temperature-related variables were the dominant predictors. Decision curve analysis demonstrated positive net benefit across much of the evaluated threshold range. Retrospective assessment suggested that approximately one quarter of antibiotic escalations and chest CT scans occurred in patients correctly predicted not to remain febrile, highlighting the potential contextual value of fever predictions. These findings indicate that short-term fever persistence can be predicted with clinically meaningful accuracy using routine data. However, clinical use should be limited to an adjunctive role rather than standalone rule-out decision-making, and prospective studies are required to evaluate safety, clinician uptake, and real-world impact.

title: Correct-and-then-detect: Adaptive fault detection through data-driven digital twins and transfer learning.
authors: Haibo Li; Zhiguo Zeng; Yang Hu; Xu Li
abstract: In a digital twin-based fault detection framework, it is essential to have a reliable and robust digital twin to generate reference values representing nominal behaviors. Traditional digital twin modeling approaches require deep understanding of functioning principles and failure mechanisms of the system, which are not always available in practice. Furthermore, as systems operate, maintaining an accurate digital twin becomes challenging as system's behavior tends to deviate from its nominal cases due to various factors like aging, uncertainty and sim-to-real gaps. To address these issues and better support predictive maintenance, this paper proposes an integrated framework for data-driven digital twin modeling and fault detection. First, we develop a design-of-experiments-based approach to generate training data that can efficiently cover the potential task space. The generated training data are then used to train a data-driven digital twin, i.e., a deep learning model that predicts system performance at a given time instant given observed covariates from a time window prior to it. Next, we develop a new adaptive fault detection method based on the developed data-driven digital twin. The algorithm works in an adaptive manner: the reference values generated by the digital twin are first compared with raw observations for residual-based fault detection. Once an abnormal observation is detected, its predicted nominal value is used to replace the corresponding observation in the internal feedback buffer before constructing subsequent context windows, thereby reducing fault-induced contamination in later predictions. Finally, a transfer learning mechanism is applied to adapt the data-driven digital twin to system's evolution and cross-domain distribution shifts using verified healthy target-domain data. Real experiments are conducted on two real robots. The results confirm that the data-driven digital twin accurately captures nominal system behavior and that the proposed framework maintains robust fault-detection performance under the considered cross-domain conditions.

title: Comparison of a quantitative MRI-based radiomics marker with semiquantitative signal alteration scores in the infrapatellar fat pad: Data from the Osteoarthritis Initiative.
authors: Adrian A Marth; Katharina Ziegeler; Gabby B Joseph; Felix Liu; Romy Zwerin; John A Lynch; Nancy E Lane; Charles E McCulloch; Michael C Nevitt; Thomas M Link
abstract:
To develop a quantitative MRI-based radiomics marker of the infrapatellar fat pad (qIPFP) based on semiquantitative IPFP signal alteration scores (sqIPFP), and to evaluate whether its associations with symptoms and imaging features of knee osteoarthritis are comparable to those of sqIPFP.
This study included 2640 participants from the Osteoarthritis Initiative, split into training (n = 2112) and test (n = 528) sets. Deep learning-based IPFP segmentation was performed on baseline intermediate-weighted fat-suppressed 3.0-Tesla MRI. Stability selection with bootstrap-resampled ElasticNet regression (≥80% selection frequency) identified radiomic features for qIPFP trained on a composite score combining sqIPFP size and intensity. Linear regression models, including age, sex, race, and body mass index as covariates, were used to compare qIPFP against the sqIPFP composite, size, and intensity scores for cross-sectional associations with the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC) pain score and Whole-Organ Magnetic Resonance Imaging Score (WORMS) scores of cartilage lesions, meniscal lesions, and bone marrow lesions (BML).
Forty stable features were included in the qIPFP marker, which showed adjusted R² values of 0.15 (95% CI 0.10-0.23) for WOMAC pain, 0.13 (95% CI 0.09-0.20) for cartilage lesions, 0.10 (95% CI 0.05-0.17) for meniscal lesions, and 0.08 (95% CI 0.05-0.14) for BML. There was no evidence of a difference compared to sqIPFP scores (all p ≥ 0.09), except for BML, where the sqIPFP composite (0.12, 95% CI 0.08-0.19; p = 0.042) and intensity scores (0.12, 95% CI 0.08-0.19; p = 0.038) yielded higher adjusted R².
A quantitative radiomics marker of infrapatellar fat pad signal alterations showed cross-sectional associations with knee osteoarthritis symptoms and imaging features comparable to those of semiquantitative scoring except for bone marrow lesions, with the advantage of fully automated, reader-independent assessment.

title: Joint segmentation of pancreatic tumors and peripancreatic vessels via a clinical risk-aware uncertainty alignment framework.
authors: Wenli Fu; Hongzhang Zhu; Tao Chen; Xiaohua Qian
abstract: Preoperative assessment of pancreatic cancer resectability critically relies on accurate joint segmentation of tumors and peripancreatic vessels from contrast-enhanced CT. However, beyond segmentation accuracy alone, effective decision support in practice further requires task-specific characterization of peri‑tumoral infiltration risk and topological discontinuity risk. To address this, we propose a clinical risk-aware uncertainty alignment framework that achieves reliable risk characterization while maintaining high segmentation accuracy. The framework is built upon a dual-decoder architecture with evidential deep learning for joint segmentation and uncertainty estimation. Two clinically grounded alignment strategies are further designed to transform this uncertainty into task-specific risk indicators. Specifically, an infiltration-aware boundary uncertainty alignment module is proposed, which synthesizes texture, spatial, and vascular proximity factors into an infiltration-inspired prior and uses its ordinal structure to guide alignment, yielding infiltration-risk-aware uncertainty from which infiltration-aware tumor boundaries are derived for downstream invasion analysis. A topology-aware discontinuity uncertainty alignment module is further designed, which uses skeleton-mismatch regions as a connectivity-related proxy and constrains uncertainty by a three-tier ordinal relation with region-weighted supervision, yielding discontinuity-risk-aware uncertainty and improved vessel connectivity. Multi-center validation on 1058 patients from five medical centers demonstrates favorable and stable cross-institutional performance, and downstream experiments explore the utility of the aligned uncertainty for tumor-vessel invasion analysis. Overall, this study couples accurate tumor and vessel delineation with clinically grounded risk characterization, with the potential to support tumor-vessel assessment in preoperative planning. Our source code will be released at https://github.com/SJTUBME-QianLab/CRUA-Net.

title: Longitudinal CT imaging to predict radiotherapy treatment outcome in head and neck cancer: a deep learning approach.
authors: Alessia De Biase; Wei Tang; Johannes A Langendijk; Peter M A van Ooijen; Nanna Maria Sijtsema
journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
abstract:
CT images acquired at multiple time points before and during radiotherapy treatment could capture tumor temporal changes, offering valuable insights into tumor response. By modeling temporal changes in CT scans with deep learning techniques, we compared the predictive performance of multi-time point models versus single time point models, assessing the impact of incorporating temporal features to predict two-year disease-free survival in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) patients.
A total of 202 OPSCC patients treated with (chemo)radiotherapy at the University Medical Center Groningen were included. A planning CT scan was available per patient, along with repeat CT scans (rCTs) acquired at different time points during treatment. Three training/ validation sets were created based on the data availability per patient: first two, three, or four consecutive rCTs. An independent testing set of 53 patients having all four consecutive rCTs was used to compare the performance of models trained using different inputs. Deep learning models were built using single or multiple time points as input. To model longitudinal features, self-attention mechanisms and temporal convolutional networks (TCNs) were applied to deep features extracted from the CT scans at different time points. Models were trained with 3-fold cross-validation and three feature extraction architectures. Predicted probabilities were ensembled by averaging. Finally, performance was assessed by accuracy, F1 macro, AUC score, and calibration plots.
Self-attention demonstrated superior ability over TCNs in capturing temporal changes in multi-time points models. The top-performing model achieved 0.75 accuracy, 0.66 F1 score, 0.61 AUC, and the best overall calibration using planning CT and the first two rCTs with self-attention. Models trained on single time point CTs up to the 10th fraction generally showed slightly lower accuracy (≤0.72), similar F1 score (around 0.66), but higher AUC (≥0.70). Despite the similar discrimination performance, TCNs demonstrated poor calibration (slope values ≥1.74).
Multi-time point CT images acquired before and early in treatment showed potential in predicting disease-free survival in OPSCC. Deep learning models based on self-attention, specifically those using planning CT and the first two consecutive rCT scans, demonstrated promising clinical utility.

title: CH₄ concentration prediction in WMS-TDLAS systems using 2f/1f signal and CNN.
authors: Wenjie Zhang; Ruoxi You; Xiaowei Li; Jianqiang Ye; Yi Wu; Ziyang Wang; Guoying Feng
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Existing deep learning-based wavelength modulation spectroscopy-tunable diode laser absorption spectroscopy (WMS-TDLAS) concentration inversion methods generally use the second harmonic (2f) signal as the model input. However, concentration-related features extracted from the 2f signal are susceptible to non-ideal factors such as laser intensity fluctuations, system drift, and baseline variations, reducing concentration inversion accuracy. To address this issue, a CH₄ concentration inversion method based on the 2f/1f signal combined with a convolutional neural network (CNN) is proposed. The 2f/1f signal is adopted as the model input to reduce the influence of system response variations and enhance the representation of concentration-related spectral information. The CNN automatically extracts nonlinear features from the 2f/1f signal and establishes the mapping relationship with CH₄ concentration. Experimental results show that, on the randomly-split test set, within the CH₄ concentration range of 0-180 ppm, the CNN model with 2f/1f input achieves better prediction performance than that with 2f input. The root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) are 0.859 ppm and 0.646 ppm, respectively, and the coefficient of determination (R2) between the average predicted and standard concentrations is 0.99999. Allan deviation analysis indicates a limit of detection (LOD) of 82.96 ppb at an integration time of 37.12 s. The results demonstrate that adopting the 2f/1f signal as input improves the concentration-inversion accuracy within the same CNN framework. Furthermore, a Kalman filter was applied as a post-processing method to suppress random fluctuations in continuous CNN prediction results and improve measurement stability.

title: Improving shear-wave speed analysis in penile vibro-ultrasound elastography using self-supervised deep learning-based IQ denoising.
authors: Ngoc Thang Bui; Matt J Ziegelmann; Tobias S Kohler; Xiaoming Zhang
abstract:
Ultrasound vibro-elastography (UVE) estimates tissue stiffness from externally induced shear waves. In cylindrical structures such as the penis, reflections and multidirectional interference produce complex wavefields that reduce acquisition reliability. The purpose of this research is to develop a deep learning-based framework to improve shear-wave speed (SWS) analysis.
A deep learning (3D U-Net) IQ-denoising framework is proposed to suppress reflected, interfering, and non-propagating wavefield components prior to physics-based inversion. The framework processes measured IQ wavefields and reconstructs SWS using the local phase velocity imaging with wave-based filtering (LPVI-WBF) algorithm. A two-stage quality-control pipeline classifies acquisitions as Good, Borderline, or Bad using thresholds τ_keep = 0.45 and τ_rel = 0.33. The network is trained on Cohort A (10 patients, 342 acquisitions) via self-supervised Noise2Self and evaluated on an independent Cohort B (6 patients, 902 acquisitions) and a simulation cohort (n = 90).
On Cohort B, deep learning (DL) rescued 376/403 Borderline acquisitions (93.3%) and preserved 89.4% of native-Good, raising the Pass rate from 38.7% to 91.8% (+53.1%). Rescued and native-Good SWS distributions were statistically indistinguishable: independent comparison (n = 227 vs 376) yielded δ = ±0.099 m/s (TOST p < 0.0001), and 198 matched pairs confirmed δ = ±0.161 m/s - both well below the ± 0.30 m/s clinical margin. In simulation, Borderline-acquisition reliability rose from 0.239 to 0.503 (n = 35; Δ = +0.264, p < 0.0001), with paired SWS equivalence at a ± 0.50 m/s margin.
Self-supervised deep learning-based IQ denoising acts as a reliability reconstructor for processing SWS data, expanding the acquisition population usable for physics-based inversion while leaving the physics-based LPVI-WBF inversion itself unchanged.

title: Artificial intelligence in sperm morphology analysis: a comprehensive review.
authors: Jing Xie; Ge Lin; Yi-Fan Gu
abstract: Sperm morphology is a crucial indicator for evaluating male fertility potential, as a morphologically normal spermatozoon is a prerequisite for successful fertilization. Consequently, sperm morphology analysis constitutes an essential component of semen analysis, aiming to assess the developmental integrity of spermatozoa. Artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly applied to sperm morphology assessment, with numerous research groups currently exploring its applications. This review provides a comprehensive overview of AI applications in sperm morphology analysis, focusing on current implementations, recent advancements, inherent advantages of AI and potential future directions. The objective is to provide a balanced assessment of both the capabilities and current limitations of these technologies, offering insights that may guide further development and facilitate future clinical translation in this field.

title: National-scale evaluation of groundwater fluoride in Ethiopia using spatially buffered machine learning.
authors: Usman Sunusi Usman; Jianmei Cheng; Bing Yan; Kuiyuan Ding; Qiang Lv; Wen Zhao
abstract: Excess groundwater fluoride (F⁻) is a public health concern in the East African Rift, yet sparse, clustered observations limit reliable national inference. This study developed a leakage-controlled framework to classify groundwater fluoride exceedance above the WHO guideline of 1.5 mg/L, separating well-level prediction from national spatial transferability. A dataset of 1567 observations, including 567 exceedances, was evaluated using five-fold buffered spatial cross-validation with a 75-km train-test exclusion radius. The hydrochemical Extra Trees model (HYD_ET) achieved the strongest well-level performance, with Macro-F1 = 0.830, balanced accuracy = 0.817, MCC = 0.671, ROC-AUC = 0.910, PR-AUC = 0.859, and Brier score = 0.116. In contrast, the environmental-only Random Forest showed negligible geographic transferability (Macro-F1 = 0.495; balanced accuracy = 0.501), while Gaussian indicator kriging achieved Macro-F1 = 0.594. Applicability-domain analysis identified 8.23% of observations outside the model domain. Because no continuous model demonstrated adequate transferability, no wall-to-wall national F⁻-risk surface was retained. Instead, 48.43%, 18.84%, and 32.73% of 10-km grid cells had stronger, moderate, and weaker monitoring support, respectively. This evaluation spans heterogeneous hydrogeological and environmental settings under uneven monitoring across Ethiopia. The results show that strong well-level prediction does not imply reliable national extrapolation and supports groundwater monitoring and data collection.

title: Automated attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder detection using an explainable EEGNet model based on electroencephalogram signals.
authors: Reza Hoseini; Ahmad Shalbaf
abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition where traditional diagnostics often suffer from subjective biases and a lack of objective biomarkers. In this study, we developed a novel, automated, and interpretable diagnostic framework using the specialized EEGNet model to extract spatio-temporal patterns directly from raw EEG signals, ensuring robust ADHD detection and model generalizability across a clinical lifespan ranging from 5 to 89 years. The primary innovation of this research lies in a specialized, lightweight EEGNet model that directly processes raw 5-second spatio-temporal EEG segments, eliminating the need for manual feature engineering or signal-to-image transformation. Our findings demonstrate that EEGNet achieves superior performance, reaching an average accuracy of 89.48% (±4.21%) and an AUC of 0.96 (±0.03), significantly outperforming the transfer learning models. A distinguishing feature of this work is the transition from black-box modeling to explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) by integrating Saliency Maps and SHAP values, which decoded the model's decision-making logic to identify key contributing channels (Fp1, Fp2, C3, T5, and A2) whose spatial attributions align with established neuroscientific literature on ADHD. The high ranking of the Fp1 (prefrontal) channel aligns with established neuroscientific evidence regarding executive dysfunction in ADHD. Furthermore, the implementation of a rigorous inter-subject evaluation demonstrates the preliminary clinical feasibility of this interpretable framework, providing a foundation for future validation on larger multi-center cohorts and offering a robust assistive tool for real-world neurological assessments.

title: Artificial intelligence in axial spondyloarthritis imaging: a review of current evidence.
authors: Lea Schumann; Lisa C Adams; Andrei Zhukov; Sandip S Joy; Finn J Kosina; Keno K Bressem; Denis Poddubnyy
abstract: The diagnosis of axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) remains challenging and is frequently delayed. Imaging is central to diagnosis, but relevant inflammatory and structural abnormalities may be subtle, heterogeneous, or overlap with findings related to mechanical stress, anatomical variation, and degeneration. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning, is therefore being investigated to support image interpretation, lesion detection, quantification, and standardized assessment. We synthesize evidence from 12 studies applying convolutional neural networks and related architectures to magnetic resonance imaging and radiographs, automate imaging scores, and combine imaging-derived information with clinical variables. Several models achieved performance comparable to experienced human readers, including during external validation. However, performance may decline in heterogeneous real-world populations for study-specific reasons not explained solely by scanner or protocol differences. No AI tool currently has regulatory clearance for autonomous use in axSpA, and applications remain largely confined to research and clinical trials.

title: Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
authors: Katane Elizabeth Kekana; Thokozani Isaac Mtshali
journal: Journal of Education and Learning Technology
abstract: Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.

title: Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
authors: Muhammad Nur Hudha; Riezky Maya Probosari; Annisa Nur Khasanah; Supurwoko; Salsabila Kholifahtun Nisa’; Gifran Rihla Gifarka Latief
journal: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science
abstract: Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored. Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes. Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement. Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization. Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.

title: A Review of Phishing Detection Techniques Using Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
authors: Dr. Sunita Dixit
journal: Journal of Global Research in Multidisciplinary Studies(JGRMS)
abstract: The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.

abstract: In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.

title: Practical Solutions to Common TAVI Complications
authors: Herbert Kroon
abstract: Aortic valve stenosis Calcific aortic valve degeneration mainly affects the elderly population. Approximately 15% of elderly patients have some degree of aortic stenosis (AS)1. Untreated severe AS will lead to heart failure, angina and/or syncope and approximately half of patients will expire within 2 years after symptom onset1, 2. Historically, open heart surgery was the only treatment for severe AS. However, advanced age was a dominant argument to defer surgery. Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) was contrived as a less invasive alternative to surgery and to fulfill this unmet clinical need. After the first-in-human procedure in 2002, TAVI matured into a guideline recommended treatment of symptomatic severe AS in elderly patients across the entire risk spectrum3-7. Peri-procedural embolization Operator experience, improved planning and implantation strategies and multiple device iterations including smaller profile, repositioning ability and outer sealing fabric converted TAVI into a reproducible and relatively safe procedure8. However, the “Big Five” of complications in the modern TAVI era remain 1) access site complications and bleedings, 2) paravalvular leakage (PVL), 3) acute kidney injury (AKI), 4) conduction disturbances including the need for permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) and 5) stroke9. Up to 5% of patients suffer a neurological event after TAVI, mainly within the first 48 hours8, 10, 11. This finding suggests a direct causative role with the transcatheter valve implantation itself. Transcranial Doppler and brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) studies revealed debris embolization towards the brain and new brain lesions after TAVI in the vast majority of patients12-15. Most of these embolizations remain clinically silent at first sight but may be linked to neurocognitive decline and frank dementia16. Embolic protection devices (EPD) have been developed to deflect or capture embolized debris on its way to the brain and may possibly reduce brain lesions and neurological events including stroke and neurocognitive decline. Part I of this thesis adds perspective to the etiopathology of TAVI related stroke and the mechanism of action of the current spectrum of cerebral embolic protection devices. We also present insights into the microscopic analysis of debris that was captured with filters during TAVI procedures. Vascular access and complications 1 TAVI typically requires large bore femoral artery access. By default, larger arteriotomies are at higher risk for access site complications and bleedings. A completely percutaneous approach relies on vascular access closure devices (VCD) to manage the arteriotomy and provide patent hemostasis. TAVI in low to intermediate risk patients is associated with a major vascular complication rate ranging between 2 and 8%4, 11. The conventional closure technique is based on sutures and most access site complications after TAVI procedures are related to closure device failure17. A collagen plug based closure device was introduced as an alternative to sutures. Part II of this thesis addresses vascular complications and provides information on clinical outcomes with collagen plug-based VCD. TAVI-related conduction disturbances Acquired conduction disturbances after TAVI are frequent and may lead to heart failure (re-) admissions and impaired long-term prognosis18-22. The atrioventricular bundle pierces the membranous septum between the right and non-coronary cusp of the aortic valve and surfaces along the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT), which makes it vulnerable to contact pressure by the implanted transcatheter heart valve (THV) during TAVI23, 24. New left bundle branch block (LBBB) and third-degree atrioventricular block (AV3B) requiring PPI occur in up to a third and quarter of patients, respectively18-22. These conduction disturbances may be transient or remain permanent which is clinically relevant in view of in-hospital stay and overall healthcare costs. Unfortunately, there are no uniform definitions to describe conduction dynamics post-TAVI. Inconsistent reporting makes the interpretation of the literature on this topic challenging. Part III of this thesis will elaborate on what is currently known about the incidence of newly acquired conduction disturbances after TAVI and studies specific features on the baseline and postprocedural electrocardiogram (ECG) to predict conduction dynamics. These insights may help determine the need and timing of PPI and adjust hospital discharge policies.

title: Myocardial remodelling during sacubitril/valsartan therapy in patients with chronic heart failure.
authors: DAVID TABUKASHVILI; V. Kapetivadze; Tamar Lazashvili; Zviadi Maglaperidze
abstract: Abstract: The aim of the study was to identify differences between aliskiren and sacubitril/valsartan in their ability to influence cardiac remodelling, metabolic balance, neurohumoral activation, and clinical symptom severity. A comparative assessment of the clinical effectiveness and impact on the structural and functional state of the myocardium was conducted for two therapeutic strategies in patients with chronic heart failure in Georgia over a 12-month follow-up. The results demonstrated fundamentally different trajectories of therapeutic response. In the sacubitril/valsartan group, early clinical improvement was observed by 6 months, including significant reductions in systolic blood pressure (-6.2%, p<0.001), respiratory rate (-4.5%, p<0.001), and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels (-10.0%, p<0.05), along with improved oxygen saturation (+3.5%, p<0.001). Left ventricular ejection fraction increased significantly already at 6 months (from 34.2±4.7% to 37.4±4.0%, p<0.001) and further at 12 months (40.5±3.5%, p<0.001), accompanied by rapid improvement in New York Heart Association functional class, with 9.3% of patients achieving New York Heart Association I by study end. In contrast, the aliskiren group exhibited slower but more pronounced structural reverse remodelling. Significant reductions in left ventricular end-systolic volume (-15.8%, p=0.009), end-diastolic volume (-17.6%, p=0.016), and end-systolic diameter (p=0.002) were observed only at 12 months, along with a modest but significant increase in ejection fraction (p=0.030). Regression of functional mitral and tricuspid regurgitation and a significant decrease in pulmonary artery systolic pressure (-19.7%, p<0.05) were more prominent in this group. Both therapies led to significant improvements in carbohydrate and lipid metabolism, including reductions in glycated haemoglobin, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and triglycerides (p<0.05 for all), indicating a favourable systemic metabolic effect. Overall, findings suggest that sacubitril/valsartan may be preferable when rapid clinical stabilization is required, whereas aliskiren may represent an effective therapeutic option for patients with advanced structural cardiac remodelling.

title: Trends in rheumatic heart disease mortality in the United States of America from 1968 to 2023: a nationwide analysis
authors: Jacky Chen; Dean Nelson; Adam Trytell; Andrew Burns; Noel Bayley; Elizabeth Davida Paratz
abstract: Abstract Background Rheumatic heart disease (RHD) is a preventable sequela of acute rheumatic fever causing chronic valvular damage to the heart. In the United States of America (USA), RHD persists among socioeconomically disadvantaged populations. This study examines long-term trends in RHD mortality from 1968 to 2023, identifying associated demographic and geographic factors to guide targeted public health interventions. Methods This retrospective observational study examined death certificate data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s Wide-Ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research (WONDER) database, encompassing three different International Classification of Disease periods (ICD-8, ICD-9, ICD-10). Analysis included stratification by age, gender, race, ethnicity and urbanisation level. Joinpoint analysis and multiple regression analysis were used to identify trends. Results RHD mortality declined significantly from 1968 to 2012, with falling crude mortality rates in both sexes and large reductions in absolute deaths among White individuals and adults aged 55–74 years. From 2012 to 2023, total deaths increased from 3,083 to 4,332, crude mortality rose from 0.98 to 1.29 per 100,000 and age-adjusted mortality increased from 0.88 to 1.04 per 100,000 (all p < 0.0001). Increases were observed across sex, race, ethnicity, urbanisation, and most age subgroups. Females had consistently higher RHD crude mortality rate ratios than men (1.09–2.43). The age distribution of RHD mortality shifted markedly over the study period, with deaths among individuals aged ≥ 75 years increasing from 17% in 1968 to 61% in 2023. Race- and ethnicity-specific CMR increased across all assessed groups from 2012 to 2023, with the largest relative increases among American Indian or Alaska Native individuals (+ 112.4%; β = 0.033 per 100,000/year, p = 0.002) and Hispanic individuals (+ 60.2%; β = 0.014 per 100,000/year, p < 0.001). Conclusion Following decades of decline, RHD mortality in the United States increased after 2012. Our study identified a persistent female predominance in RHD mortality and a marked shift in mortality burden from middle-aged adults towards older populations.
